name: Hume AI Octave
positioning: Hume's Octave is a speech-language-model text-to-speech API with prompt-based voice design and acting instructions; Hume's documentation says its TTS and EVI APIs are being sunset, with access ending on 13 November 2026.

pricing.model: Monthly subscriptions with included characters and per-character overage rates on the higher plans; one subscription covered TTS, EVI and voice features. The live pricing page now redirects to the homepage, so no current price list is available to cite.
pricing.headline: Hume's pricing page is no longer on its site (the address redirects to the homepage as of 2026-10-10). The only copy we found is an Internet Archive snapshot dated 2026-09-01, so this page shows no Hume prices.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Non-commercial use only (docs FAQ). 15 requests per minute. The billing docs also mention USD 20 in credits for new accounts.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.notes: Non-commercial only; no overage purchase (upgrade required). Effective USD 100 per 1M of included allowance.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.unit: USD 14 per month (USD 7 first month); 140,000 characters; USD 0.15 per 1,000 after
tiers.notes: 75 requests per minute. Effective USD 100 per 1M of included allowance at USD 14. Overage rate on the first paid tier with a commercial license, from an archived snapshot of hume.ai/pricing (2026-09-01); single-source, live page removed.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.unit: USD 70 per month; 1,000,000 characters; USD 0.12 per 1,000 after
tiers.notes: 75 requests per minute. Effective USD 70 per 1M of included allowance.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.unit: USD 200 per month; 3,300,000 characters; USD 0.10 per 1,000 after
tiers.notes: 150 requests per minute. Effective about USD 60.6 per 1M of included allowance.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.unit: USD 500 per month; 10,000,000 characters; USD 0.05 per 1,000 after
tiers.notes: 225 requests per minute. Effective USD 50 per 1M of included allowance.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Custom limits; API voice access listed.

pricing.freeTier: Free plan: 10,000 characters per month (archived pricing page); non-commercial use only.

voices.languages: Octave 1: English and Spanish. Octave 2 (preview): English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, German, Russian, Hindi, Arabic.
voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Voice design from a text description; voice cloning from as little as 15 seconds of audio (availability depends on subscription tier).

streaming.vendorStatedLatency: Vendor-stated: Octave 2 (preview) ~100 ms and Octave 1 ~200 ms model latency, not including network transit; instant mode first audio typically within ~200 ms.

compatibility.note: Hume exposes its own endpoints (/v0/tts, /v0/tts/file, /v0/tts/stream/json, /v0/tts/stream/file, and WebSocket /v0/tts/stream/input) with utterance objects containing text, voice, description and speed.

licensing.commercialUse: Commercial use was allowed on Creator and above; Free and Starter were for non-commercial use.
licensing.attributionOrConditions: Users retain rights to output; Hume receives a perpetual licence to use voice recordings and voice models to provide and improve services. Use must comply with Hume's prohibited-use policy.

limits.perRequestCharacters: 5,000 characters per utterance; description up to 1,000 characters; up to 5 generations per request
limits.concurrency: HTTP rate limits are set by subscription tier; the per-tier figures were on the pricing page that has since been removed.

compliance.note: Self-attested in the Compliance row of the archived pricing page (Enterprise column): SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA. Not re-checked on a live page because the pricing page was removed.

strengths.claim: Octave is built on a language model, and the docs describe it adapting delivery to the emotional meaning of the text.
Voice design from a plain-language description, plus acting instructions to steer delivery after a voice exists.
Streaming over HTTP and WebSocket, with word and phoneme timestamps and a continuation feature to keep consistency across long-form text.
Octave 2 (preview) lists 11 languages including Japanese, Korean, Hindi and Arabic.
Users retain ownership of audio they generate.

limitations.claim: Hume's documentation says it is sunsetting the TTS and EVI APIs: access ends 13 November 2026, and account data is permanently deleted afterwards.
Free and Starter plans were limited to non-commercial use.
Octave 1 lists two languages, English and Spanish; the broader language list is on Octave 2, which is labelled preview.

stepsToMove: Plan the move before the 13 November 2026 shutdown date stated by Hume; account data is deleted afterwards, so export anything you need first.
If you also use Hume's EVI speech-to-speech API, it ends on the same date; this checklist covers the text-to-speech API, not EVI.
Hume authenticates with an API key (the SDK reads HUME_API_KEY); replace the SDK client with the target service's client.
Replace /v0/tts, /v0/tts/file or the streaming endpoints (/v0/tts/stream/json, /v0/tts/stream/file) with the target's equivalents; WebSocket users replace /v0/tts/stream/input.

Map each utterance (text, voice name or id, description, speed, trailing_silence) to the target's request fields; description-based voice design and acting instructions have no direct equivalent in most services.
Re-create cloned voices on the target from the original consented audio, and re-test output format needs (MP3, WAV or PCM).

mapping.vendorItem: POST /v0/tts and POST /v0/tts/file (generate audio in one response)
POST /v0/tts/stream/json and POST /v0/tts/stream/file (streamed audio over HTTP)

mapping.note: Re-create any cloned voice from its original consented audio where the target allows it; ReadAloud lists no Hume voices

mapping.vendorItem: utterances[].description (acting instructions and voice design text)

bestFor: Teams that were using Octave for expressive, prompt-designed voices; because Hume has announced the API's shutdown on 13 November 2026, new projects should plan around that date.

statusNote: Hume's own documentation (dev.hume.ai/voice/intro and the Text-to-Speech overview, read 2026-10-10) says it is sunsetting the TTS and EVI APIs, with access ending 2026-11-13 and account data deleted afterwards.

sunset.notice: Hume is sunsetting the TTS and EVI APIs. Access ends November 13, 2026 at 12:01 a.m. EST
sunset.dataDeletion: Any data in your account is permanently deleted after November 13, 2026.
